content_voiceover: This slide summarizes malignant germ cell tumors, or MaGCT, which arise from primordial germ cells and can show up in a surprisingly wide range of locations. The most common primary sites are gonadal, the testes in boys or the ovaries in girls, but you also need to know the extragonadal sites, abdomen, mediastinum, the sacrococcygeal area, which is the classic site in infants, and intracranial, particularly the pineal and suprasellar regions. Pathologically these tumors span a spectrum, yolk sac tumor, mixed germ cell tumor, choriocarcinoma, and teratoma, which can be immature or mature. The key special exam is checking tumor markers, elevated beta-H C G and or A F P, and on the next slide you'll see exactly which marker goes with which histologic subtype. Treatment depends heavily on histology, primary site, and stage, but generally involves chemotherapy and surgery, with radiotherapy used selectively, and autologous stem cell transplant reserved as a salvage option for relapsed or refractory disease. The overall prognosis is genuinely reassuring, five-year survival varies with stage and histology but overall outcome is excellent, which is an important reassurance point for boards, since these tumors, despite sounding alarming, are among the more curable pediatric solid tumors.
keypoints: Most common sites: testes (boys), ovaries (girls); also sacrococcygeal, mediastinum, intracranial
Histologic spectrum: yolk sac tumor, mixed GCT, choriocarcinoma, mature/immature teratoma
Special exam: tumor markers, elevated beta-hCG and/or AFP
Treatment: chemotherapy plus surgery, selective radiotherapy, auto-HSCT for salvage
keypoint_voiceover: Malignant germ cell tumors most commonly arise in testes or ovaries, but also occur sacrococcygeally, mediastinally, and intracranially. Histology ranges from yolk sac tumor to choriocarcinoma to teratoma, and diagnosis leans on beta-hCG and AFP. Treatment is chemotherapy plus surgery with auto stem cell transplant reserved for salvage, and overall prognosis is excellent.
